title: Understanding KDE Plot
text: A KDE plot is used to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. It can help visualize the distribution of data points.

title: Kernel Choice in KDE
text: The choice of kernel in a KDE plot affects the smoothness and shape of the estimated distribution. Different kernels can highlight different features of the data.

hintAnswer: A normal kernel might smooth out the data too much, making distinct peaks less visible.
title: Identifying the Issue
text: Why might a normal kernel not be suitable for visualizing multimodal data?
choices: A normal kernel might smooth out the data too much, making distinct peaks less visible.
A normal kernel is always the best choice for any data.
A normal kernel highlights multimodal features effectively.

hintAnswer: Epanechnikov, Tophat, or Gaussian kernels can be used to better visualize multimodal data.
title: Exploring Kernel Options
text: What are some alternative kernels that could be used to better visualize multimodal data?
choices: Epanechnikov, Tophat, or Gaussian kernels can be used to better visualize multimodal data.
Only the normal kernel can be used.
Any kernel will produce the same result.
